title: Scene of the Crime
text: “From what I heard after the fact, apparently this Takt guy let Wolf win a bunch of matches before finally throwing a big-money bout to make him lose. More like a match-fixing scheme—totally an inside job kind of setup, I bet.”
“Real piece of work, that guy,” Father spat venomously.
Heh. A creature doomed to suffer for all eternity, indeed. Sin had finally been repaid with punishment!
“I’d heard the rumors, saね. Well, fighters win some and lose some, so it doesn’t do any good getting worked up over it, saね.”
“Speaking of which, what kind of win rate do Lars-chan and the others have, I wonder?”
“Naturally, if they’re popular, it’s high, saね.”
“That’s right. They rarely lose, which is exactly why they’re popular, and depending on the season, they even earn through sponsorship deals.”
“Father, Father. There was a loop where I entered too and became a popular fighter, I say.”
The Filolial Mask, indeed. Kweh, if you will.
“If you never lose, becoming famous is pretty easy indeed.”
“Well, I doubt there’s anyone who could beat Motoyasu-kun.”
“And here Sadeena wonders what would’ve happened if we’d crossed paths back then, saね.”
“That was right after we got through the first wave in Melromarc, so I don’t think we’d met Panda and the others yet, indeed.”
Timing-wise, weren’t we still in Siltvelt around then? If we’d met, I’d surely remember.
“Elephant was probably away at the time too, I think… but since we hadn’t actually met yet, there’s no way to be certain, I say.”
Father did become a famous merchant in Zeltoble around then, after all. So there’s a chance we crossed paths there later on. Though that was quite a while ago, so it’s all rather hazy now.
“I’d hate to think we had met him back then… he’d probably have left me unable to fight ever again.”
“Well, Older Sister used to go drinking at the taverns in Zeltoble, so I’m sure she and Panda and the rest became acquainted.”
“Ugh, no thanks… being dragged along by that drunk.”
“But she’s good company, isn’t she? You end up remembering her naturally, and you can tell she’s strong.”
“That’s certainly true, saね. Well, to begin with there are the open matches and the underground ones, so it depends which you weight more, saね.”
“Which type do Lars-chan and the others usually fight in, I wonder?”
“No one lasts long as a regular in the underground bouts, saね.”
“There are some matches down there that are practically fights to the death, so we don’t enter lightly. Though if you’re popular, it pays decently well.”

Indeed, the underground matches in Zeltoble are mostly a rich man’s indulgence, that’s true. In that sense, back when I was raking in fortunes underground, I likely rarely ran into Panda and the others. By the way, I was often called in specifically to deal with Takt whenever he went around stirring up trouble in the underground matches. Once Father became an executive in Zeltoble, my appearances in the underground matches dropped off—apparently I was winning too much, so adjustments were made. If anything, I seem to recall being given work capturing dangerous monsters meant for the underground bouts instead.
“It’s a good country to lie low in, isn’t it.”
“Can’t argue with that, saね.”
“This is all well and good, but are we there yet?”
“Is it far?”
“Voff. We’ll arrive soon.”

And so we finally arrived at what could only be described as the ruins of some stone church. Abandoned, most likely? Though it looked like some makeshift cloth had been strung up, enough to sleep under.
“Monster sightings around here—that’s the job this time… voff.”
“Right. Let’s go find the monster we’re after, then.”
“It’d be nice if we could sense something by presence alone.”
“Can’t you find it with those ears of yours?”
Crocodile Guy asked Rabbit Guy. Heh. If I were an usaunny, I could pick up sound from a wide area too, I say.
“If you’re going to say that, you sense your surroundings through presence-detection or whatever too, don’t you?”
“True enough. But strange presences… I don’t know this land, so I can’t really tell.”
“Voff… before we split up to search, I want everyone to stay together.”
It seemed something unpleasant awaited Wolf here. He trembled faintly beside Father, tail drooping, refusing to move. Father, sensing something was off about him, quietly took his hand.
“Hmm…”
“I wonder what it is. If there’s a reason, I wish he’d just say so… though somehow, I feel like I can guess.”
Rabbit Guy seemed to have picked up on something. Crocodile Guy nodded once as well, as if he had some idea too.
“I haven’t the faintest clue, I say.”
“Well, of course you wouldn’t, Motoyasu-kun.”
“Well, anyone who’s been listening can pick up on it at least a little… but I suppose some folks just don’t, saね.”
“Quiet, I say!”
“Yuki doesn’t get it either, wahー!”
We’re the type who needs things spelled out, indeed!
“Not sure what good declaring that does…”
Well then, Wolf, let’s go… Father said, seeming to understand, giving Wolf gentle instructions. And all the while, he was quietly holding his hand.
“…Voff.”
Encouraged by Father, Wolf began to walk.
“That’s the tricky thing about him, isn’t it.”
“Truly…”
Rabbit Guy and Crocodile Guy looked like they were grumbling about Father.
“Anyway, nothing to do but go, saね. Onward we go.”
“Yes, that’s right.”
“I wonder what’s there~”
Kou’s carefree, cheerful voice seemed to liven up the whole group.
“Father and the others aren’t answering me, I say.”

What was there, I wondered? To my question, Father and the rest simply walked on without answering, leaving me no choice but to follow. And so, where Wolf led us… we arrived at a place littered with snapped and fallen trees.
“V-Voff…”

Traces of some attack, perhaps? Much of it looked weathered by time, but the marks were still clearly visible. Piecing together the earlier conversation, this was likely where Wolf’s brother had trained. Wolf stopped at one corner of the clearing and sank to his knees.
“……It was here that my brother had his claws stolen by Takt, and was killed.”
Ah, I see… so this was the scene of Takt’s crime.
“……I see.”
Father nodded as though listening closely to Wolf’s words.

“That day, Takt showed up with that woman who has a bounty on her head, and suddenly attacked my brother without warning. We’re both Heroes—there was no reason for us to fight! But then… my brother glared at that woman, and Takt brought his companions with him and…”
“He was after the claws, and I’m guessing he was helping that bounty woman get her revenge here.”
“Voff.”
“Seriously, what a hardened criminal. Now that the truth’s come out, I think your brother’s regrets can finally be laid to rest. So don’t let it weigh on you.”
At Father’s words, Wolf silently shook his head.

“Voff… that’s not it. I… back then, when my brother had his claws stolen and fought back but couldn’t even scratch them, I was so scared I lost the strength in my legs… and even when my brother realized he was outmatched and ordered me to run, I couldn’t do anything.”

Wolf said this in a grief-stricken voice, gazing at the claws in his hands, tears creeping into his tone. It would be unfair to call it pathetic, given how high the levels of Takt and his pig cronies were. Even I was forced into a full retreat the first time I ran into Takt. There’s no seeing the future, after all—nothing to be done about it. But having meddled in the pasts of various pigs over the years and done all sorts of things because of it, I’m hardly one to mock him for it. Though in my case it was usually a pig, wasn’t it? Wolf is male, though. I suppose that’s just one of the rules of this world I ended up in. If this had happened back in the Japan I came from, would Wolf have turned out to be a pig instead, I wonder?
“Even so, my brother leapt at them bravely despite being outmatched… and then their dragon’s flames left nothing behind. I was so afraid… if only I’d fought back then…”
Ah, this was it. This was the moment where cheering him up was the proper move, indeed. Surely Father would know exactly what to say without me even mentioning it, wouldn’t he?
